clue.text: Make too many copies of stamp

definitions.meaning: to print more than are needed
to print an extra marking over an existing postage stamp design

explanation.surface: A philatelic forger churns out too many copies of a stamp.
explanation.definitionFit: Printing beyond the run required is excess printing; a surcharge printed across a postage stamp is also called this.

clue.text: Run past in striking football kit

parts.note: workers who are striking are out
a team's playing kit is its strip in British football

explanation.surface: Someone sprints past while wearing an eye-catching football kit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'striking' looks like 'eye-catching' but means on strike, OUT; a football team's kit is called its STRIP in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: To outrun a rival is to get ahead of them, overtaking them.

clue.text: Run more than usual

definitions.meaning: in cricket a run not scored off the bat, such as a wide or bye
additional, over and above the normal amount

explanation.surface: A runner pushes on further than they normally would.
explanation.definitionFit: Cricket's byes and wides are runs credited outside the bat; the adjective means additional.

clue.text: With the same rapidity as Priapus, unfortunately

indicators.note: an unfortunate turn of events suggests these letters have gone wrong and must be rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Something moves just as quickly as the Greek fertility god Priapus, sadly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unfortunately' rearranges AS with PRIAPUS; 'as' looks like a link word but is part of the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin phrase means at an equal pace, side by side, equally.

clue.text: One paid a premium for his work?

definitions.text: One paid a premium for his work?

parts.words: One paid a premium for his work?
parts.note: reads like a well-rewarded worker, but a premium is the regular payment made to an underwriter for cover

explanation.surface: A craftsman is paid a bonus for the quality of his work.
explanation.definitionFit: An underwriting company receives premiums from policyholders in return for cover against loss.

clue.text: What one may enter below?

parts.note: a window over a doorway sits above the person walking in underneath

explanation.surface: A question about what lies beneath a point of entry.
explanation.walkthrough: A TRANSOM is the crossbar, or the small window above it, over a door, so you go in beneath it.
explanation.definitionFit: The horizontal bar or fanlight above a door is passed under by anyone coming in.

clue.text: American president leads a maiden to one side?

indicators.note: the president is placed in front of the remaining pieces, leading them

parts.note: Abe is Abraham Lincoln, the US president
M is the cricket abbreviation for a maiden over

explanation.surface: Lincoln escorts a young woman off to the side.
explanation.definitionFit: On a ship, this means at right angles to the keel, level with the vessel's side.

clue.text: Round of applause has no place in examination

indicators.note: the praise word lacks the abbreviation for place, so those letters are dropped

parts.note: a plaudit is an expression of praise, a burst of clapping

explanation.surface: An ovation is out of place during an exam.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has no' takes PL out of PLAUDIT.
explanation.definitionFit: An official inspection of accounts is a formal examination of them.

clue.text: Essential manifestation of the powers of nature

definitions.text: manifestation of the powers of nature
definitions.meaning: a spirit embodying earth, air, fire or water

explanation.surface: A phrase describing the essential display of nature's forces.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means fundamental, and as a noun names a spirit of one of the four classical elements.

clue.text: Power can be provided by having this flex

definitions.text: Power can be provided by having this flex

parts.words: Power can be provided by having this flex
parts.note: reads like an electric cable carrying current, but the thing flexed is a body part giving strength

explanation.surface: Electricity is supplied through a flexible cable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flex' is the British word for an electric cable, which sets up an electrical picture; here it is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Contracting tissue gives the body its strength, and its name is also slang for force or clout.

clue.text: Book private teacher

explanation.surface: A request to hire a teacher for private lessons.
explanation.definitionFit: An instruction manual for a musical instrument bears the same name as a coach giving one-to-one lessons.

clue.text: Old university at Reading literally spreads all around

annotationWithheld.why: Old university at Reading literally spreads all around (2,7): STREWS (spreads) around AND gives ST ANDREWS, but no parse found for how 'at Reading literally' supplies AND; scan confirms the wording and a search found no explanation
annotationWithheld.clue: Old university at Reading literally spreads all around

clue.text: One striking about right for one to catch foxes?

indicators.note: the striker goes about, around, the abbreviation for right

parts.note: a tapper strikes lightly

explanation.surface: A hunter strikes about for the right moment to catch foxes.
explanation.definitionFit: A fur hunter sets snares and gins to catch animals such as foxes.

clue.text: Poet that's fashionable outside Italy

indicators.note: the stylish word goes outside, around, the code for Italy

parts.note: swell is old slang for smart or stylish
IT is the international code for Italy

explanation.surface: A trendy poet keeps clear of Italy.
explanation.walkthrough: SWELL is dated slang for smart. Edith, Osbert and Sacheverell were poet siblings of this surname, so any of them fits 'Poet'.
explanation.definitionFit: Edith of that surname was an English modernist poet, as were her brothers.

clue.text: Millions run Indian cities, strangely confused

indicators.note: something done strangely is out of the usual order, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: M is the abbreviation for million(s)
R is the cricket abbreviation for run(s)
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Millions of people run Indian cities, in strange confusion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'strangely' rearranges M, R, INDIAN and CITIES.
explanation.definitionFit: Something haphazard and random, showing no discrimination, is jumbled and muddled.

clue.text: Place for bopping and getting drunk in France, that has heroin and everything

indicators.note: a drunk staggers about, so the letters of the word before are jumbled

parts.note: ce is French for that
H is slang for heroin
everything means all

explanation.surface: A nightclub in France where people get drunk, take heroin and do everything.
explanation.definitionFit: A venue for bopping is a public room for dancing.

clue.text: Take daft name Saint regularly used of Petran kingdom

parts.note: to nab is to take or seize

indicators.note: taking every other letter of the following words, at regular intervals

explanation.surface: A daft name is used of a saint in an ancient kingdom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' takes the 2nd, 4th, 6th... letters of DAFT NAME SAINT: A, T, A, E, A, N.
explanation.definitionFit: The ancient Arab realm with its capital at Petra gives its people's name as an adjective.

clue.text: One making a living from icings and toppings?

definitions.text: One making a living from icings and toppings?

parts.words: One making a living from icings and toppings?
parts.note: sounds like a cake decorator, but icing and topping are both slang for killing someone

explanation.surface: A baker earns a living decorating cakes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'icing' (US slang) and 'topping' (British slang) both mean murdering.
explanation.definitionFit: A hired killer earns a living from murders.

clue.text: Blair man is in US, having arranged an excellent time

indicators.note: the letters are put into a new order, arranged differently

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Tony Blair's aide in America has organised a wonderful time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arranged' shuffles BLAIR MAN IS IN US.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin phrase names a year of wonders, a remarkably successful period.

clue.text: Gas that a stunned Macbeth might have breathed near cauldron?

definitions.text: Gas that a stunned Macbeth might have breathed near cauldron?

parts.words: Gas that a stunned Macbeth might have breathed near cauldron?
parts.note: split as '...?', Macbeth's amazed question when the witches at their cauldron hail him Thane of Cawdor

explanation.surface: Macbeth inhales fumes from the witches' cauldron.
explanation.walkthrough: In Shakespeare's play, the witches greet Macbeth as Thane of Glamis and Cawdor; 'Gas' points to the marsh gas.
explanation.definitionFit: Marsh gas is the simplest hydrocarbon, and the clue's breathed phrase splits to spell it.

clue.text: What provokes a response concerning a man

parts.note: re means about or concerning
a gent is a gentleman, a man

explanation.surface: A question about what makes a man react.
explanation.definitionFit: A chemical substance added to cause a reaction is a reactant.

clue.text: Edit a paper to be published

indicators.note: editing changes a text, so these letters are reworked into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An editor prepares a newspaper for publication.
explanation.definitionFit: A book is said to come out when it is issued in print.

clue.text: Offered excuse before writing

parts.note: pre- means before
a text is a piece of writing

explanation.surface: Someone made an excuse before putting anything in writing.
explanation.definitionFit: A false reason given to hide the real one is a cover story.

clue.text: Start to experiment with worthless type of resin

indicators.note: the start of the next word means its first letter only

parts.note: poxy is British slang for worthless, rubbishy

explanation.surface: A beginner experiments with a cheap kind of resin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Start to' takes the first letter of 'experiment'. POXY is British slang for useless.
explanation.definitionFit: A tough thermosetting polymer used in glues is a synthetic adhesive resin.

clue.text: Girl going about this island could reveal giant iguana

indicators.note: the girl's name joins the answer and the pair is jumbled, turned about, into the clue's phrase

parts.note: the composite's full pool; the island's name also runs unbroken inside these two words, a bonus beyond coincidence that 'could reveal' plays on, though the girl's role makes the composite the parse
Gina is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A girl touring an island might come across a giant iguana.
explanation.walkthrough: A composite anagram: GINA plus the answer, rearranged ('going about'), gives GIANT IGUANA, and 'could reveal' also points to giANT IGUAna, where the island sits in plain sight.
explanation.definitionFit: The Caribbean island in the Leeward group is the place the clue points to.

clue.text: Maxim among writers

parts.note: reads like a saying passed around authors, but Maxim is the first name of a Russian novelist

explanation.surface: A saying that circulates among authors.
explanation.walkthrough: Maxim GORKI (also spelt Gorky) was the Russian author of The Lower Depths.
explanation.definitionFit: The Soviet novelist and playwright went by the forename Maxim.

clue.text: Soldiers troubled after old pain returns with complications

indicators.note: the soldiers and their trouble come after the reversed pain word
returns means the word for old pain is read backwards

parts.note: bale is an archaic word for woe or suffering
OR, other ranks, is the usual crossword abbreviation for soldiers
ate, as in 'what's eating you?', means troubled or worried

explanation.surface: Troops fret after an old injury flares up and becomes complicated.
explanation.walkthrough: BALE is an archaic word for woe, found mainly in crosswords and old verse; ATE as 'troubled' comes from 'what's eating you?'.
explanation.definitionFit: Something detailed and intricate is complicated.

clue.text: Gains points after listening

indicators.note: the compass points come after the listening word

parts.note: an ear is the organ of listening, and being 'all ear' is attending
N and S are compass points

explanation.surface: Someone scores points after paying attention.
explanation.definitionFit: To receive money for work is to be paid, to gain.

clue.text: Revive competition among drivers

definitions.meaning: to refresh with a new supply, as a fresh team of horses replaces a tired one
a race in which team members take over from one another in turn

explanation.surface: An instruction to restart a motor race.
explanation.definitionFit: A fresh set of horses on a coach route, and a team race run in stages, share the name.

clue.text: Prolongation of former strained relations

parts.note: ex- means former
tension is strain between people

explanation.surface: A drawn-out period of strained relations with a former partner.
explanation.definitionFit: A lengthening in time, such as more days granted, is a prolonging.
